answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity via cryptographic attestation chains verified through zero-knowledge proofs. While genuine nodes pass validation like a gentle zephyr, an adversarial swarm faces exponential capital exhaustion: registration staking scales superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot 2^n$. The vast ocean of required collateral creates an impassable economic canyon, making swarm replication computationally and financially ruinous.
